topic: Solving Linear Inequalities in One Variable
title: Why Does the Sign Flip? Inequalities Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Two is less than five. Put a minus sign on both and minus two is now bigger than minus five, as any freezer shows. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 5, Linear Inequalities) we learn how to solve a linear inequality in one variable and why the arrow flips.

You will see the two NCERT rules (add or take away the same number, multiply or divide by the same positive number), then watch a live multiplier slide from 1 to -1 so two points squeeze through zero and swap sides: the reason the sign reverses for a negative number. We solve 4x + 3 < 6x + 7 step by step with its number line, work NCERT Exercise 5.1 Question 10, and look at the exam trap where students flip for no reason. A pause-and-think question, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

In this video:

2:36 Solve 4x + 3 < 6x + 7 step by step
3:16 Worked example: NCERT Ex 5.1 Q10
3:56 Exam trap: flipping when you should not
4:30 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:08 Recap and three questions to answer
